summary: The memuneh held a second lottery to choose who would do each job for the korban tamid: shechting, sprinkling the blood, cleaning the inner mizbe'ach and the Menorah, and carrying up each part of the korban.
stIntro: Four lotteries were conducted in the Temple each day in order to determine which priests would perform which of the Temple rites. After describing the first of the lotteries, for removal of the ashes, the tanna describes the second lottery.

chunks.en: The memuneh said to them,
chunks.st: The priest appointed to oversee the lotteries said to the priests:

chunks.en: "Come and join the lottery, (to see):
chunks.st: Come and participate in the lottery to determine

chunks.en: who shechts (the korban tamid),
chunks.st: who is the priest who will slaughter the daily offering;

words.note: Slaughters the animal the kosher way.

chunks.en: who sprinkles (its blood),
chunks.st: and who is the priest who will sprinkle its blood;

words.note: Throws the blood on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: who cleans the ashes off the inner mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: and who will remove the ashes from the inner, golden altar;

chunks.en: who cleans the ashes out of the Menorah,
chunks.st: and who will remove the ashes from the Candelabrum;

chunks.en: who brings the parts (of the korban) up to the ramp:
chunks.st: and who will take the limbs of the daily offering up to the ramp
chunks.stMore: to be burned afterward. The limbs of the daily offering taken up to the ramp were divided among the priests in the following manner: One priest took

chunks.en: the head and the (right back) leg,
chunks.st: the head and the right hind leg up to the altar;

chunks.en: and the two front legs,
chunks.st: and a second took the two forelegs;

chunks.en: the tail end and the (left back) leg,
chunks.st: a third the haunch, including the lower spine and the tail, and the left hind leg;

chunks.en: the chest and the neck,
chunks.st: a fourth the breast and the cud,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the neck and appended internal organs, including the windpipe, liver, and heart;

words.note: The neck with the windpipe and some inside parts.

chunks.en: and the two sides,
chunks.st: and a fifth the two flanks;

chunks.en: the insides, and the flour,
chunks.st: a sixth the innards; and a seventh the fine flour from the accompanying meal offering;

words.note: Fine flour of the mincha that comes with the korban.

chunks.en: and the chavitin, and the wine."
chunks.st: and an eighth the griddle-cake offering; and a ninth the wine for the libation.

words.note: The flat flour offering of the Kohen Gadol.
Wine poured on the mizbe'ach with the korban.

chunks.en: They held the lottery, and whoever won, won.
chunks.st: They conducted the lottery to determine the thirteen tasks, i.e., slaughtering, carrying the nine items or pairs of items, sprinkling the blood, removing the ashes from the inner altar, and removing the ashes from the Candelabrum. And whoever won that lottery won
chunks.stMore: the right to perform the slaughter, and the twelve priests standing to his right won the other privileges.

summary: Before shechting the korban tamid, the memuneh sent someone to check if it was daytime yet. The one who looked would call out when the sky in the east was light.

chunks.en: The memuneh said to them,
chunks.st: said to the priests:

chunks.en: "Go out and see if the time for shechting has come."
chunks.st: Go out and observe if it is day and the time for slaughter has arrived.

chunks.en: If it had come,
chunks.st: If the time has arrived,

chunks.en: the one who looks says,
chunks.st: the observer says:

chunks.st: There is light. Matya ben Shmuel says
chunks.stMore: that the appointed priest phrased his question differently, saying:

words.note: It is light!
A Kohen who was the memuneh.

chunks.en: "Is the whole east lit up
chunks.st: Is the entire eastern sky illuminated

chunks.en: all the way to Chevron?"
chunks.st: as far as Hebron?

words.note: A city south of Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: And he says, "Yes!"
chunks.st: And the observer says: Yes.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: said to the priests:

chunks.st: Go out and bring me a lamb from the Chamber of the Lambs,
chunks.stMore: where lambs that had been examined and found to be unblemished were kept.

chunks.en: The Room of the Lambs was
chunks.st: And the Chamber of the Lambs is located in the

chunks.st: took out from there ninety-three

chunks.st: silver vessels and gold vessels.

chunks.st: who won the privilege of the removal of ash from the

chunks.st: From Jericho the people would hear the sound indicating
